meta.title: Stroke Rehabilitation | Cambridge Hospital
meta.description: Restoring movement, speech and independence after stroke.

overview: A stroke can change a person’s life in an instant, affecting movement, speech, swallowing, cognition and emotional well-being. Timely, intensive rehabilitation is the single most important factor in how much function a patient regains.

At Cambridge Hospital, we run a structured post-stroke pathway that begins as soon as a patient is medically stable, progressing through inpatient rehabilitation, outpatient therapy and home care follow-up. Our programme combines gait and balance training, repetitive task-specific exercises, speech and language therapy, swallowing assessments and occupational therapy, with family education integrated throughout so that gains made in therapy carry over into daily life.
